world.label: LOS ANGELES 1937
world.title: Silver Nitrate
world.blurb: Meridian's vault registrar is found among the negatives, the count unfinished. Every columnist in town prints the stars' secrets by dark — and about this death, printed nothing.
tuning: Chandler's rain on Hammett's bones: the glamour is a painted flat, and the wiring behind it is live.
Every scene smells of cigarette smoke, developer chemicals, orange blossom, or money.
The pictures lie for a living and the town believes them anyway — the only real magic in it.
Nitrate remembers everything and forgives nothing. Say so without saying so.

ledger.A: The Angel of Crenshaw — a nun, a pistol, and a producer who prayed too late.
ledger.C: Chinatown Nocturne — pulled from release the week the real detective sued.
ledger.E: The Eleventh Reel — a serial whose ending no surviving print still carries.
ledger.G: Graveyard Shift — shot nights on a cemetery set the city later paved.
ledger.H: Hollywood Confidential — the negative burned the week the columnist vanished.
ledger.I: The Iron Ingénue — her contract outlived her; the studio kept billing the part.
ledger.L: Lot Thirteen — a backlot-fire picture; three grips never came off the call sheet.
ledger.O: The Orphan Reel — a film the vault lists and no living eye has seen.
ledger.P: Pacific Wardrobe — a costume drama that drowned its lead and reshot around her.
ledger.S: Sunset Salvage — a repossession comedy the bank did not find funny.
ledger.T: The Ten-Cent Tenor — a musical dubbed by a man the credits never name.
ledger.U: Under the Marquee — a Depression weepie; the theater it played is a parking lot.
ledger.V: The Velvet Alibi — a courtroom picture the front office used to launder a real one.

openingLines: The searchlights come on at dusk over the boulevards and rake
the underside of the clouds for premieres that mean nothing to
anyone east of La Brea. Meridian Pictures makes dreams by day
and keeps them in a fireproof vault by night, because dreams on
silver nitrate burn hotter than gasoline and remember more.
This week the vault lost the man who kept its count.
{VICTIM} knew every negative that went in and came out, and was
found at the door of Vault C with the tally open and unfinished.
Every columnist in town prints the stars' sins by dark — and
about this one, they printed nothing. Bought silence develops
clearest in a town this bright.
Four names held the keys to the front office. Three trails will
cut them down to one: the coin, the keys, and the one witness
nobody ever thought worth paying to look away.
